The rules are easy and can be learned by almost anyone within a minute or two. You can push 1, 2, or 3 marbles at a time. Your marbles can move 1 space, either in a straight line or laterally. And the last rule: you need 2 marbles to push 1 opponent marble, while 3 marbles lets you push 1 or 2. And that's it! Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Gameplay 14 marbles per player are placed on a 6 size hexagonal board. Black moves first. On your turn, each player may move either a marble or a column of marbles one space in any direction. If the move is in-line, marbles are moved as a column into free space. If the move is side-step, they are moved sideways. When a player's column faces an adjacent opponent's column with fewer marbles and it is not sandwiched (sumito), they can push one marble 1 space. They may choose to push two if the column has 3 marbles. At any turn, no more than 3 of your marbles can move. So any column larger than 3 is not in a sumito. Marbles pushed out of the rim are captured and are not in play. End of the Game The player who first pushes 6 opponent marbles off the board wins. Variants Setup: Two extra different setups, named Belgian Daisy and German Daisy, are available. [Rating: 1/10] Once you know how to play you can play for a draw every game. There is also a way to break the game. the first person to attack always looses if you know how to play. Concepts is great, game fails to implement it and enough opening move variations.

[Rating: 1/10] The first player wins almost all of the time unless they are foolish. What kind of a design is that?

[Rating: 1/10] I hates it. If no one player begins to attack the game is last forever and ever and ever and ever...

[Rating: 1/10] That this is essentially a broken game has been pointed out often enough. The bits are nice, though - I use my set to play a hex-version of "Lines of Action", which is great fun!

[Rating: 1/10] Strategy is way too static and defensive. I can't remember a player ever making a move that made either person excited or really react in any way.

[Rating: 1/10] Terrible. Maybe I'm missing something, but this seems like it is just "race to the middle". There seems to be no way to interact with someone who has a giant clump in the center. As with many capture games, if you fall behind then you will start to lose harder. Perhaps there is a bait-and-switch strategy here; I'd rather play Blooms for that. Really bad even when compensating for the year it was released

[Rating: 2/10] With two even players this can degenerate into effective stalemate. My brother and hour had one game last hours until exhaustion/tedium got the better of me and I made a slip from which it was not possible to recover.

[Rating: 2/10] Fundamentally broken as an abstract game.  This is like Sumo - with the wrong rules, that the wrestlers can freely touch the ground with any parts of their bodies.  Thus, unless the opponent is so overwhelmingly strong enough that he can just lift you up and toss you out of the ring, any person who can sit or lie down becomes unbeatable.  It's an exciting sport if the wrestlers stand and fight, but charging against a sitting opponent will always bring defeat, so why bother.  A "2" instead of "1" (or "0") only for the components.

[Rating: 2/10] Abalone is a game with nice components both visually and aurally (the clacking when a large move is made is pleasing.)  It's the only reason it isn't a 1.  The only problem is the game completely drawish.  To those who say this a great strategy game--here's a hint.  Form a compact group with your pieces and try to force your way to the center.  And NEVER EVER EVER get foolish and actually try to attack.  The only way to lose is to try to win.  And if you never try to win, you can never lose.  Tournament setup only change it to a race for the center.  Still not a great game.

[Rating: 2/10] The wife played well but after a while it felt like a stalemate as we just pushed each other around on the board until somone (me!) got bored and played risky and then lost.  But then maybe I just didn't know how to play well.

[Rating: 2/10] After about 5 plays I realized that this wasn't a game.  You win by waiting for the other player to try to do something, and then you beat him for it.

[Rating: 2/10] The game, while having gorgeous components and a pleasant clic-clac mechanism to lock the marbels in place, is not fun to play if you set it up in its standard position: it becomes a matter of keeping your group of marbles together longer than the other player. This extremely defensive style dulls the game to a nearly unplayable degree. I always meant to try and play this game with a variant of sorts, but I never had the heart to do so. At some point, I simply gave it away. and I regret to say it shall not be missed.

[Rating: 2/10] I am not into Abstract Strategy game. It's not my favorite mechanic/theme. I find it to be not to my liking compared to other game mechanics. There are better Abstract Strategy games out there than Abalone. Yinsh is a whole lot more to my liking than Abalone for example.  I wouldn't say no to trying other Abstract Strategy games.  It wasn't really interesting for a 2 player abstract. Wasn't fun either. It's not my kind of game. It didn`t really impress me. [Rating: 2/10] I just don't love it. Gift is similar and more fun... but I just don't like abstracts 2-players games.

[Rating: 2/10] The shiny components invites to play but the game is boring and feels like it would never end with the persisting deadlock.

[Rating: 2/10] Dry, boring abstract game. The marble pieces are awesome. Easy rules. The main problem is this: it is actually very easy to play defensively and between equally-skilled players the game can last for hours. Anyway the game seems out-dated by many other abstract games.

[Rating: 2/10] 1 / 5 - Bad.  Abstracts aren't really my thing. Super-defensive abstracts with a high probability of stalemate are really, really not my thing.

[Rating: 2/10] This game seems like my type of game. I love 2 player abstracts. The pieces feel nice in hand, the design is simple and the gameplay even seems clever. But the best strategy in this game is to never approach. Too boring.
